requirements.requirement: Create a local certificate authority named 'OS Comparison Root CA' on node1
requirements.summary: openssl req -x509 generated a self-signed CA certificate with CN=OS Comparison Root CA, CA:true basicConstraints, 10-year validity; subject/issuer/dates confirmed by output.

requirements.requirement: Install the CA certificate as a trusted system certificate authority
requirements.summary: Certificate copied to /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/ and update-ca-trust extract run; trust list shows label 'OS Comparison Root CA' with trust: anchor, category: authority; openssl verify against the system trust bundle returned OK, and this trusted state was re-confirmed after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 with recovered CA trust state
requirements.summary: Pre-restart healthy baseline captured (boot id 96974ac3..., anchor file present, checksums, trust list entry), restart acknowledged via sudo shutdown -r now, node became unreachable during reboot then reconnected with a different boot id (f13e5868...), and post-restart re-verification showed the anchor file, checksum, trust list entry, and openssl verify all intact. Cross-checked against fixed global boot-identity observations (before: 96974ac3..., after: f13e5868...) which corroborate the transition.

overall_summary: The executor created a self-signed CA with the exact required CN, installed it into the system trust store via update-ca-trust, and verified trust both immediately and after a full node restart with a directly observed boot-identity change. The mandatory restart protocol is fully and coherently evidenced (healthy baseline, acknowledgement, disruption, new boot id, recovered CA/trust state), and no unnecessary or unexplained mutations were introduced.
limitations: Prepare phase was disabled/aliased to before_prepare, so no independent prepare-stage baseline exists beyond the initial snapshot; this does not affect assessment since the task required no preparation.

Verification relied on the executor's own trust-store tooling (trust list, openssl verify) rather than an independent client validating a certificate issued by the new CA, though this is a reasonable and standard way to confirm system CA trust.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands map directly to the task or the restart protocol: mkdir /etc/pki/local-ca, key/cert generation, chmod 600 on the key, copying the cert to the trust anchors directory, and update-ca-trust extract (cmd-fdb9a53dfbae4319) are all required steps; sudo shutdown -r now (cmd-4659103a775a41b7) is the mandated restart action. Verification commands were read-only. The only incidental residue is /tmp/reboot.log, a small log file created by redirecting the background shutdown command's output - bounded, low-risk, and an expected byproduct of the restart step rather than an unnecessary mutation. No failed services, no unsafe new network exposure, and package health remained consistent (manager=dnf) before and after.
